title: Maple-Glazed Pork Tenderloin with Sweet Potatoes
subtitle: seared pork tenderloin roasted with a sticky maple-garlic glaze, beside caramelised sweet potato chunks
imageAlt: Sliced maple-glazed pork tenderloin with roasted sweet potato chunks on a white plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Oven at 220°C (425°F). You need an oven-safe skillet for the pork.
Trim the thin, shiny silver skin off the tenderloins with a sharp knife; it turns chewy.

items.name: sweet potatoes
items.note: about 2 large, peeled and cut in 3 cm chunks

items.name: pork tenderloins
items.note: about 500 g each, silver skin trimmed

steps.title: Sweet potatoes in
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, salt and cinnamon on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet and roast 35–40 minutes, turning once, until caramelised at the edges.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Pat the pork dry and rub with the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce, vinegar and garlic together.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high and brown the tenderloins on all sides, 6–8 minutes in all.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Pour half the glaze over the pork and move the skillet to the oven. Roast 12–15 minutes, brushing with the rest of the glaze halfway, until the centre reads 71°C (160°F).

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Move the pork to a board and rest 8 minutes. Set the skillet over medium (the handle is hot), stir in the butter and simmer the pan glaze 1–2 minutes until syrupy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Slice the pork 1.5 cm thick, spoon the glaze over and serve with the sweet potatoes.

fixIt.fix: Add a splash of water to the skillet as it goes into the oven; maple burns quickly on bare metal.
Tenderloin is lean; pull it at 71°C (160°F) and rest it. A blush of pink is fine.
Spread them out so they don't touch and roast on the upper rack.

saleTip: Pork tenderloin 2-packs are a regular No Frills deal; freeze one for another night.
swap: Honey instead of maple syrup: same amount.
leftovers: Slice cold for sandwiches, or reheat gently with a spoon of water.
doneness: 71°C (160°F) in the centre (Health Canada, pork); a faint blush of pink is fine. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested maple-glazed pork tenderloin methods (Canadian Living, Ricardo): seared tenderloin finished in a 220°C oven with a maple-soy glaze, rested to 71°C.
prepAhead: Trim and season the pork up to 1 day ahead.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes the night before; keep them covered in the fridge.
reheat: Slices covered in a skillet over low with a spoon of water 3–4 minutes, or in the microwave 1 minute, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Salt-and-pepper pork with a maple and soy glaze; plain roasted sweet potatoes.

stepNotes.5: Basic: skip the butter; spoon the glaze straight over.

fancy.note: A toasted pecan crumble over the sweet potatoes.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: for the last 5 minutes, scatter the pecans over the sweet potatoes and drizzle with the extra maple syrup.

plating: Sweet potatoes piled alongside, pecans on top.
Pan glaze in a little jug.

why.1-0: Tenderloin is the leanest, most tender pork cut and cooks in under 25 minutes.
why.2-2: A splash of vinegar keeps the maple glaze from tasting flat and too sweet.
why.0-3: A pinch of cinnamon brings out the sweet potatoes' natural sweetness.

funFact: Canada produces about three-quarters of the world's maple syrup, most of it in Quebec.

keeps.note: freeze sliced pork in its glaze

drink: A Pinot Noir or an off-dry Riesling, or apple cider.
